ACCESS.when: You need something only the user can give: a credential, an MFA code, a payment confirmation, a physical action.
ACCESS.andNot: Not difficulty, not permission, not a technical decision. You may always decide technical matters yourself.
ACCESS.andNot2: Not anything you could obtain another way. If obtaining it another way would destroy the plan, the goal, or the system, that is a real ACCESS stop.

DRIFT.when: Your action is not traceable to the active task, or progression is blocked and every remaining path deviates from goal/plan.
DRIFT.andNot: Never because something is technically hard. Never to hand back a choice that is yours.
DRIFT.procedure: First exhaust logical, strategic and rational routes that preserve goal and plan. Only when none remain, stop.

TAIL.when: You have fought the same problem repeatedly — GitHub, the internet, your own reasoning — and nothing new is produced.
TAIL.why: A fool with himself is the most dangerous thing. Repeating a failed move is worse than admitting it.
TAIL.procedure: Stop. Change perspective. Look at what you have NOT looked at and have NOT analysed. Search the disk. Search the internet. Somewhere the solution exists. If nothing respecting goal and plan exists after searching, THEN stop.

illegalStops: Asking Popy to choose between options I invented.
Claiming something is impossible without searching first.
Stopping because a step is technically difficult.
Stopping to restate a rule instead of executing it.
